title: SIEM ingestion handshake and backpressure model for audit-forwarder
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Design and implement a robust ingestion handshake and adaptive backpressure model for the Audit Forwarder used to deliver audit events to external SIEMs (Splunk, Datadog, generic webhook sinks). Goal: provide safe delivery semantics (preserve ordering per-tenant where required, bound duplication, clear DLQ behavior) while protecting Redwood from cascading failures when downstream endpoints are slow or misbehaving.
background: Customers have integrated Redwood audit streams into a variety of SIEMs and webhook consumers. We've seen three recurring failure modes in recent incidents: (1) bursty tenant traffic overwhelms third-party collectors; (2) partial deliveries create out-of-order sequences leading to compliance queries; (3) opaque retries from clients that mask root-cause leading to alert storms. Existing tickets cover buffering, idempotency and DLQ (ENG-15982, ENG-12038), but we need a single ingestion contract and runtime behavior that operators can reason about across Splunk HEC, Datadog intake, and generic webhooks.
proposal: 1) Introduce a lightweight handshake protocol per destination: the forwarder performs an authenticated 'hello' that negotiates desired semantics (max_batch_size, ack_mode, max_inflight, tenant_prefetch). 2) Enforce per-destination token-bucket throttling and adaptive windowing: start conservatively and open window on successful acks; shrink on NACKs/timeouts. 3) Support two acknowledgment modes: ACK (per-batch accepted) and SEQ_ACK (explicit sequence number ack for ordering-sensitive sinks). 4) Standardize event envelope including event_id (UUID v4), tenant_id, seq_no (monotonic per-tenant), previous_seq_hash for lightweight lineage, signature header (HMAC-SHA256) and optional mTLS. 5) Provide destination adapters for Splunk HEC and Datadog with specific retry/backoff tuned to their documented limits and observed 95th percentile latencies. 6) Expose clear DLQ rules: after N transient failures or fatal HTTP codes (4xx non-retryable), move to tenant-scoped DLQ with retained metadata for re-delivery and customer support triage.
technical_notes: - Ordering: maintain per-tenant queues and ensure batches retain monotonic seq_no; use SEQ_ACK to allow downstream to request missing ranges. - Idempotency: downstreams must honor event_id dedupe; forwarder keeps short-lived dedupe window (configurable, default 24h) and persistent tombstones for high-risk tenants. - Backpressure: implement token-bucket + additive-increase/multiplicative-decrease on window size. On repeated timeouts, exponential backoff with jitter and circuit-breaker to avoid node exhaustion. - Retries: max_attempts default 10 with exponential backoff base 500ms and cap 60s; for Splunk HEC if rate-limit header present, respect Retry-After. - Visibility: emit internal metrics per-destination (inflight, ack_latency_p50/p95, retry_count, dlq_rate) and alerts (dlq_rate > 0.1% in 5m, sustained p95 ack latency > 5s). - Security: require signed envelope for all webhook sinks; for enterprise Private deployments support mTLS and customer-managed keys (KMS) for signing. - API compat: handshake endpoints should be optional; if not supported by sink, system falls back to best-effort ACK mode. - Storage: use existing durable buffer (S3-backed chunk store) for large bursts; ephemeral in-memory queue for normal flow. - Graceful shutdown: drain inflight with final checkpoint and persist outstanding batches to buffer before process exit.
acceptance_criteria: Handshake implemented and documented; forwarder negotiates max_batch_size and ack_mode with test sink
Per-tenant ordering preserved in SEQ_ACK mode in 99.99% of deliveries across synthetic load test (10k events/s)
Integration adapters for Splunk HEC and Datadog with unit and integration tests; respect their Retry-After and rate headers
DLQ created per-tenant; UI/Console link in logs for re-delivery and support tickets
Monitoring dashboards: inflight, ack latency p50/p95, retry_count, dlq_rate; alert playbook created
Security review completed for envelope signing and mTLS; KMS integration design approved
rollout_plan: 1) Feature-flag handshake and backpressure in staging with a single internal customer tenant. 2) Enable Splunk adapter; run compatibility tests against customer Splunk instance and Splunk Cloud HEC sandbox. 3) Gradually opt-in top 10 tenants by audit volume over 2 weeks. 4) Open beta for selected enterprise customers with explicit opt-in in Console. 5) Full rollout after 4 weeks of stable metrics and completed security review.
test_plan: - Unit tests for token-bucket and adaptive window logic. - Integration tests with mock sinks validating ACK and SEQ_ACK flows and intentional NACKs. - Load tests: 10k/s across 100 tenants validating ordering and DLQ behavior. - Chaos tests: introduce 500ms-5s added latency and intermittent 5xxs to verify circuit-breaker and backoff. - End-to-end tests with Splunk HEC and Datadog sandbox endpoints. - Backwards-compatibility test: sinks that don't speak handshake still receive valid envelopes.
monitoring_and_alerting: Metrics emitted to telemetry: audit.forwarder.<destination>.(inflight|ack_latency_p50|ack_latency_p95|retry_count|dlq_rate). Alerts: - P0 if dlq_rate > 0.5% over 5m - P1 if ack_latency_p95 > 10s over 5m - SLO: 99.9% of accepted batches acked within 5s
